Extract model estimates and analysis results

Source: R/get-data.R
get_results.Rd

get_results() returns one table of a fitted model, an enumeration grid, a comparison, a bootstrap test, a starting-value set or a diagnostics result as a data frame, chosen by name with what. Without what it returns the object's primary table (the same as as.data.frame()), and with what = "all" a named list of the tables the object builds by default. The catalogue below gives each table's rows, columns and arguments. Many tables also have a verb of their own that takes any object, such as get_entropy(), get_avepp(), get_best() or get_tree().

Usage

get_results(x, what = NULL, ...)

Arguments

x

A fitted model of this package, an enumeration grid, a model comparison, a bootstrap comparison, a starting-value set, a diagnostics result, or the summary of any of them.

what

Name of the table, or "all". NULL (default) gives the primary table: the measurement model of a fit, the candidates of a grid, the test row of a bootstrap comparison, the entropy table of a diagnostics result. An unknown name is refused with the names the object offers.

...

Arguments of the requested table, named in its catalogue entry and described under Table arguments; a table refuses any other.

Value

A data frame for one what, or a named list of them for "all". "all" builds each table with its defaults and leaves out the tables this object cannot produce (a sequence table of a fit without time, for example) and those that must be asked for ("lmr", "recovery"), so the names of the list say what was available. Every object also has print(), summary() (taking level and vcov_type where the model has standard errors) and as.data.frame().

Tables of a profile, class or transition fit

"profiles"

The Gaussian measurement model, one row per profile and continuous indicator: profile, indicator, mean, variance, standard_deviation, mean_standard_error, variance_standard_error. Takes scale and data.

"responses"

The categorical measurement model, one row per profile, indicator and category: profile, indicator, category, probability, threshold (qlogis(P(y <= category)), NA for the last category), probability_standard_error. Takes data.

"covariances"

One row per profile and ordered pair of continuous indicators: profile, indicator, indicator_2, covariance (exact zeros off the diagonal under a diagonal structure).

"ordinal", "count_means"

The ordinal and count measurement models of fits with such indicators. Take data.

"local_dependence", "direct_effects"

For fits with those arguments. Local dependence has pair, kind, profile, item_1, category_1, item_2, category_2, probability, independent, ratio, covariance, correlation: a categorical pair has one row per profile and category combination with the joint probability, the product of the marginals (independent) and their ratio; a continuous pair one row per profile with covariance and correlation. Direct effects have one row per effect: indicator, covariate, estimate, standard_error, statistic, p_value, conf_low, conf_high.

"counts"

Effective class sizes (summed posteriors), one row per level and class: level, class, effective_count, effective_proportion.

"model", "information_criteria"

One row describing the fit: dimensions, likelihood, parameter counts, criteria, convergence and boundary status; "information_criteria" has the same columns for every family and takes format and definitions (see Information criteria).

"posteriors"

One row per observation and profile: row, group, profile, posterior, modal. Takes format. Excluded observations keep their rows with NA.

"group_posteriors"

One row per group and group class: group, group_size, log_likelihood, group_class, posterior, modal. Takes format.

"assignments"

One row per observation: the columns the fit was built from (or those of data), profile, group_class where there is one, uncertainty (one minus the posterior of the assigned profile), one posterior_profile_* column per profile, and posterior_noise for a noise fit (profile 0). Takes data and truth; with truth it returns a recovery table (see Recovery). Rows with no observed indicator have NA assignments under drop_empty = TRUE, but keep a group class supported by other rows.

"classification"

One row per level and class: level, class, n_modal, proportion_modal, estimated_n, estimated_proportion, average_posterior, odds_correct_classification. Takes level. See Classification quality.

"average_posteriors"

For the units assigned to each class, their mean posterior for every class: level, assigned_class, class, n_assigned, average_posterior; rows sum to one within an assigned class. Takes level.

"classification_errors", "bch_weights"

The probability that a unit of one true class is assigned to another (level, true_class, assigned_class, probability), and the BCH weights that invert that matrix (level, unit, assigned_class, class, weight). Take level. On a covariate fit they are marginal over the units; not available for a noise fit.

"entropy"

One row per level: level, n_classes, n_units, entropy_sum, relative_entropy.

"replication"

One row: n_starts, n_screened, n_converged, n_failed, n_best_replicated (starts within tolerance of the best log likelihood), share, tolerance, best_start, log_likelihood.

"starts"

One row per start: start, log_likelihood, converged, iterations, error, boundary where recorded, and under search = "emEM" kind, stage ("final" or "screened") and screened_log_likelihood.

"residuals"

Bivariate residuals of every indicator pair: profile, indicator_1, indicator_2, kind, observed, expected, residual, effective_n, statistic, df, p_value, p_adjusted. Takes data, by and adjust. See Bivariate residuals.

"gaussian_diagnostics"

One row per Gaussian component: context, profile, gaussian_mass, positive_rows, weight_effective_n, min_variance_ratio, min_standardized_eigenvalue, boundary: how much posterior mass a component carries, how concentrated it is, and how small its variances are relative to the data. Descriptive, with no cutoff and no effect on start selection.

"sequences", "sequence_summary"

Fits with time: the assignments in occasion order (group, group_class, time, profile; takes format) and one row per group class (group_class, groups, observations, mean_length, median_length, shortest, longest, complete, gaps).

"data"

The data the model was fitted to, in input order: the identifier, the occasion, the rescaled weights and the indicators under their original names; not the covariates, so three_step() and r3step() take data.

"profile_probabilities", "stages"

A multilpa fit: one row per group class and profile (group_class, profile, probability, group_class_probability), and one row per estimation stage (stage, group_classes, fixed, log_likelihood, parameters, parameters_with_measurement, converged; two rows for a fit_staged() result).

"coefficients"

A covariate fit: one row per membership coefficient (level "profile" or "group", outcome, term, parameter, always "logit", estimate); standard errors come from parameter_inference().

"transitions", "initial", "sequence_lengths"

A transition fit: one row per group class and ordered pair of profiles (group_class, from, to, probability, expected_count, stable, estimated, origin_expected_count, supported, group_class_probability; takes estimated and stable); one row per group class and profile (group_class, profile, probability, prevalence, group_class_probability); one row per group (group, group_class, occasions, observations, complete).

Under sampling weights every population quantity, here and in the grid tables, is weighted: effective and estimated counts and proportions, average posteriors, the odds of correct classification, entropy, classification errors, BCH weights, the criteria and the tree's mass; modal counts stay unweighted counts of the units of positive weight. A unit of weight zero keeps its row and posteriors in the assignment and posterior tables but enters no statistic.

Tables of an enumeration grid

"candidates"

One row per candidate: candidate, its class counts and model, log likelihood, parameter count, every criterion under both sample-size conventions, both entropies, the AvePP summaries of each level (avepp_min, avepp_max, avepp_mean, avepp_below, and the same with group_), convergence, boundary, replication, the Gaussian diagnostics, warnings and error. Failed candidates keep their row. Takes cutoff (default 0.8) for avepp_below; a class with no assigned unit counts as below it. get_candidates() drops the columns empty in every row.

"best"

One row per criterion and convention: criterion, convention, candidate (the converged candidate with the lowest value), n_profiles, n_group_classes, model, value. "criteria" is its older name, still in "all".

"classification"

One row per fitted candidate, level and class: candidate, its class counts and model, the columns of a fit's "classification" table and the level's relative_entropy.

"deltas", "knees"

Model-selection evidence, taking using (default "bic_groups"); neither selects a model. "deltas" has one row per candidate: candidate, n_profiles, n_group_classes, model, criterion, value, delta_profile (the decrease from the converged candidate with one profile fewer; positive means this one is lower) with from_profile, and delta_group_class with from_group_class; NA where the neighbour is missing or unconverged. "knees" has one row per line of the grid (direction "profiles", "group_classes" or "parameters", line, criterion, from, to, n_points, knee_candidate, distance, knee_without_largest, stable, note): the candidate furthest below the chord of the line, a simplified Kneedle rule; a line needs three candidates for a knee and four for stable.

"tree"

The flows of plot_tree(), taking its arguments n_group_classes, n_profiles (n_classes on a regression grid), model, candidates, from, to and level (default "individuals"). One row per pair of classes in consecutive rows of a tree: tree, level, from_candidate, from_class, from_share, to_candidate, to_class, to_share, mass (the share of all units the two classes share, summed over the products of their posteriors), share_of_from, share_of_to.

"lmr"

The Vuong-Lo-Mendell-Rubin and adjusted Lo-Mendell-Rubin tests, one row per pair of converged candidates differing by one profile or one group class at the same structure: direction, null_candidate, alternative_candidate, the alternative's class counts and model, n_units, parameters_added, lr, vlmr_p, adjusted_lr (lr / (1 + 1 / (parameters_added * log(n_units)))), almr_p, reference_mean, reference_sd and note. The reference is a weighted chi-square with the eigenvalues of Vuong's matrix as weights, evaluated by Imhof's method; a pair with a singular information matrix or a boundary candidate keeps its row with NA and the reason in note. Built only when asked for.

A transition or family grid has "candidates" (with one entropy and no AvePP summaries), "best" (taking criterion: "bic", "aic" or "bic_individual") and "tree" (not in its "all"). The models of a grid or a comparison are extracted with get_candidate().

Tables of the other objects

A compare_models() result: "comparison" (its table) and "classification" (one row per model, level and class, for profile, class, covariate and transition models). A bootstrap_lrt() result: "test" (one row) and "replicates" (one row per simulated data set). A starting-value set: "profiles", "responses", "profile_probabilities" and "covariances". A diagnostics() result: "entropy", "classification", "average_posteriors", "residuals", "replication" and "checks".

The other model families return their own tables, the first being the default. Tables with intervals take level and vcov_type ("observed", "robust" or "opg"; NULL reuses the type stored with a regression fit).

Mixture regressions

"coefficients" (one row per class and term with Wald statistics, p_adjusted by Benjamini-Hochberg over the non-intercepts, and exp_estimate where the link makes it an odds or rate ratio; intercept ratios are NA), "classes", "membership" (logits and odds ratios), "group_classes" (two-level fits), "fit" (bic on the rows under observation nesting and on groups under group or two-level nesting, bic_rows on the rows), "assignments", "groups", "fitted" (ordinal observations, fitted values and residuals use category scores 1,...,C), "starts" (stage "screened" or "completed"), "classification" and "recovery" (by = "class" or "group_class"). Identifier columns that collide with output names use an id_ or cluster_ prefix, with a unique suffix if needed.

Growth mixtures

"coefficients", "classes" (share with its interval, expected_persons, assigned_persons, average_posterior, residual_sd), "membership", "fit", "assignments" (one row per person: class, probability, one posterior_* column per class), "starts", "recovery", "random" (variances, standard deviations and correlations of the random effects, with intervals on the log and Fisher scales), "random_effects" (one row per person), "trajectories" (each class's mean curve with a band) and "individual" (each person's curve); the last two take time. A multilevel growth mixture adds "group_classes" and "clusters", and its "fit" has bic on the clusters and bic_persons on the persons.

Additive fits

"parameters" (class means, between- and within-group variances and class weights, with variance intervals on the log scale and weight intervals on the logit scale; takes adjust, "none" by default), "group_classes" (with effective_groups, the number of perfectly classified groups that would estimate the class weight as precisely; below 50 the class's intervals warn), "groups", "intercepts", "conditional_intercepts", "assignments", "classification", "fit", "recovery" and "starts".

Cross-level fits

"profiles" (the profiles, then the group classes' means of group means), "group_classes", "composition" (profile shares within each class: model-implied for the full family, a posterior-weighted description for the restricted one), "groups", "assignments", "fit" and "starts". The likelihood is a working likelihood that counts the ratings twice: its criteria favour group classes and the full form even with no group structure, and do not choose between them.

General transition fits

An lta() fit with occasion-specific or covariate transitions, occasion-specific measurement, second order, a stayer class, weights, or ordinal or count indicators: "transitions", "initial" and "second_order_transitions" (model-implied, averaged over the groups and applicable occasions), with origin_expected_count and supported describing transition-row information, "transition_coefficients", "initial_coefficients" and "second_order_coefficients" (log odds with odds ratios), "profiles", "covariances" (under covariance_model = "full"), "responses" (with occasion), "ordinal", "count_means", "group_classes", "assignments", "posteriors" (with format), "entropy", "information_criteria" (with format and definitions; one entropy per level, as for the other transition fits), "fit" and "starts". profile is "profile_1", ... in "profiles", "responses" and the transition tables, and the profile's number in the others.

Pooled imputations

"estimates", "imputations" (each imputation's aligned estimates) and "fits" (one row per imputation).

Table arguments

data

One row per observation of the fit, in the fitted order; NULL uses the columns the fit carries. The standard errors of "profiles" and "responses" come from parameter_inference() on these data; a fit that cannot supply them gives NA with a message when data is omitted, and raises the condition when it is given.

scale

For "profiles": "raw" (default) or "standardized", each indicator's deviation from its grand mean in units of the observed population standard deviation. Weighted fits use a weighted mean and spread, excluding zero-weight rows; unweighted fits use the same population convention.

format

For the posterior tables and "sequences", "long" (default, one row per unit and class) or "wide" (one row per unit). For "information_criteria", "wide" (default, one row) or "long" (one row per criterion and convention).

level

"individuals", "groups" or "both"; NULL (default) is "both" for a fit with group classes and "individuals" otherwise.

truth

For "assignments", column names of data holding known labels. See Recovery.

by, adjust

For "residuals": "profile" (default) or "overall", and the multiplicity correction across the pairs ("none" by default, or a stats::p.adjust() method).

definitions

For "information_criteria" in long format, TRUE adds each criterion's formula and reference.

estimated, stable

For "transitions", TRUE or FALSE keeps the rows estimated (or not) from observed occupancy, or the diagonal (or off-diagonal) cells.

Recovery

"assignments" with truth cross-tabulates the model's labels against known ones: one row per class and truth value, with assignment (the label compared: group_class for a truth constant within every group of a fit with group classes, profile otherwise), class, truth, value, n and proportion (the share of units with that truth value assigned to that class). Excluded units appear under class = NA. Labels are arbitrary, so a truth value assigned mostly to a class with another label is relabelling, not misclassification.

Information criteria

With q free parameters, n the sample size and EN the entropy of the classification: deviance = -2L, aic = -2L + 2q, bic = -2L + q log(n), sabic = -2L + q log((n + 2) / 24), caic = -2L + q (log(n) + 1), awe = -2(L - EN) + 2q (1.5 + log(n)), icl = -2L + q log(n) + 2 EN, kic = -2L + 3(q + 1) (as tidyLPA computes it) and clc = -2L + 2 EN (on the entropy sum, so not comparable with tidyLPA's CLC on relative entropy). EN is the soft entropy of the complete-data classification, as in ICL, AWE and CLC; in a two-level model it is the group-class entropy plus each row's profile entropy within its group class.

Every criterion with a sample size is reported under two conventions, "groups" (n the number of groups) and "individuals" (n the number of rows), which coincide in a single-level model; use one consistently across candidates. A transition fit keeps one entropy per level instead, since its profiles form a chain within a person. Rows with no observed indicator, groups made only of such rows, and units of weight zero are in no sample size and no entropy. The long format with definitions = TRUE reports each formula.

Classification quality

The odds of correct classification of a class is (p / (1 - p)) / (r / (1 - r)), with p the average posterior in the assigned class and r the estimated class proportion: near one, the classification is no better than the class proportions; five is a conventional benchmark, not a test. It is NA when p is missing or zero or r is zero or one (so always for a single class), and Inf when p is one at an interior r. relative_entropy is 1 - entropy_sum / (n log K), with entropy_sum the level's own entropy, between zero and one, higher meaning sharper classification; NA for a level with one class. A fit without group classes reports individuals only.

Bivariate residuals

"residuals" checks, pair by pair, that the indicators are independent within a profile, weighting each observation by its posterior. Two Gaussian indicators (kind = "gaussian"): observed is the posterior-weighted residual correlation, expected the correlation the fitted covariance implies, and statistic the difference of their Fisher transforms times sqrt(effective_n - 3), referred to the normal distribution. Two categorical or ordinal indicators ("categorical"): statistic is the Pearson chi-square of the posterior-weighted two-way table against the model's, Latent GOLD's bivariate residual times its df = (R - 1)(C - 1), with observed and expected the two tables' Cramer's V; the reference ignores that the model's table is estimated from the same data and can be conservative. A mixed pair or a pair with a count indicator ("mixed", "count"): observed is the posterior-weighted correlation of the values (a categorical indicator entering as its category number), expected zero, and no test. p_adjusted applies adjust (Benjamini-Hochberg by default, "none" for the raw p-values) across the pairs with a p-value. A weighted fit reports the descriptive columns and no tests.

See also

as.data.frame() for the primary table, summary() for every table, diagnostics() for the classification tables with their checks, and the verbs get_checks(), get_entropy(), get_classification(), get_avepp(), get_residuals(), get_replication(), get_candidates(), get_best(), get_deltas(), get_knees() and get_tree().

Examples

fit <- multilpa(
  course_engagement,
  vars = c("browse", "lectures", "forum_read", "forum_post", "attendance"),
  id = "student", n_profiles = 2, n_group_classes = 2, n_starts = 4,
  seed = 1
)
get_results(fit)
#>    profile  indicator       mean  variance standard_deviation
#> 1        1     browse  0.5395774 0.5898715          0.7680309
#> 2        1   lectures  0.4274031 0.8446923          0.9190714
#> 3        1 forum_read  0.6198249 0.4814743          0.6938835
#> 4        1 forum_post  0.5304888 0.6887895          0.8299335
#> 5        1 attendance  0.6490498 0.3841263          0.6197793
#> 6        2     browse -0.7655998 0.5284684          0.7269583
#> 7        2   lectures -0.6064852 0.5383733          0.7337392
#> 8        2 forum_read -0.8792137 0.3631130          0.6025886
#> 9        2 forum_post -0.7526883 0.4211624          0.6489703
#> 10       2 attendance -0.9206599 0.3736293          0.6112523
#>    mean_standard_error variance_standard_error
#> 1           0.02710160              0.02948401
#> 2           0.03248649              0.04210054
#> 3           0.02473030              0.02439626
#> 4           0.02953027              0.03481645
#> 5           0.02226482              0.01955858
#> 6           0.03121144              0.03221700
#> 7           0.03093059              0.03209025
#> 8           0.02621510              0.02279295
#> 9           0.02768122              0.02607600
#> 10          0.02642702              0.02278996
get_results(fit, what = "profile_probabilities")
#>   group_class profile probability group_class_probability
#> 1           1       1   0.1704508                0.325297
#> 2           1       2   0.8295492                0.325297
#> 3           2       1   0.7859317                0.674703
#> 4           2       2   0.2140683                0.674703
get_results(fit, what = "entropy")
#>         level n_classes n_units entropy_sum relative_entropy
#> 1 individuals         2    1422   60.939978        0.9381731
#> 2      groups         2     106    4.434661        0.9396428
names(get_results(fit, what = "all"))
#>  [1] "profiles"              "responses"             "covariances"          
#>  [4] "gaussian_diagnostics"  "profile_probabilities" "counts"               
#>  [7] "posteriors"            "group_posteriors"      "assignments"          
#> [10] "classification"        "average_posteriors"    "classification_errors"
#> [13] "bch_weights"           "entropy"               "replication"          
#> [16] "residuals"             "information_criteria"  "model"                
#> [19] "stages"                "starts"                "data"                 

# Compare estimated assignments with the generating classes at both levels.
get_results(fit, what = "assignments", data = course_engagement,
         truth = c("engagement", "student_type"))
#>    assignment class        truth      value   n proportion
#> 1     profile     1   engagement disengaged  16 0.02735043
#> 2     profile     2   engagement disengaged 569 0.97264957

#> 4     profile     2   engagement    engaged  17 0.02031063
